title: Araripe green run input, version 1
description: What one green run deposits under runs/<run_id>/ so that publication can proceed without a git pull request. This document is the operator's command line written down: it carries exactly the information scripts/publish_green_release.py takes as --ledger, --artifact, --product, --date, --state-sha256 and --state-bytes, and nothing else. It is NOT a second ledger and defines no scientific fact: every checksum a publication trusts still comes from the processing ledger this document points at. Intent is declared here, never deduced from bytes.

run_id.description: The immutable per-run prefix this document lives under: runs/<run_id>/. One path segment, so a run identity can never address another run's prefix.

ledger.description: Where the processing-ledger-v3 document sits inside the run prefix. Fixed, exactly as the release manifest fixes its own ledger path: a run that needs a second name for it is publishing two things.

persistence_state.description: Provenance of the persistence state this run wrote — a digest and a length, never a claim about its contents. In particular max(last_seen) is not a watermark: update_tracks moves it backwards inside the 16-day window (GREEN_RELEASE_CONTRACT_V1.md §4).

logical_path.description: Path inside the release prefix. No absolute path, no traversal, no backslash, no trailing slash. Identical to the release manifest's rule, because this becomes that.

path.description: The logical path this object will occupy inside the release prefix.

source.description: Where the bytes sit inside the run prefix. Same path rule, so a source can never escape runs/<run_id>/.

kind.description: acquisition_artifact: the object IS the artifact whose checksum the ledger row seals. date_product: derived for a whole UTC date, and the ledger makes no claim about it. Declared, never inferred from a checksum — a first draft of the 2B.2B CLI guessed this and let a tampered artifact pass as another kind of object.

observed_on.description: The UTC date this object belongs to. Declared rather than parsed out of the path: a filename is not evidence of anything.
